<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XV.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|183}}</noinclude>found it, laieth it vpon his shoulders reioycing: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=6}}† and comming home calleth together his frendes and neighbours, saying to them, Reioyce vvith me, because I haue found my sheepe that vvas lost? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=7}}† I say to you, that euen so there shal be ioy in heauen vpon one sinner that doth penance, {{sup|‖}} then vpon ninetie nine iust that neede not penance. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=8}}† Or vvhat {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This woman is the catholike Church, vvho also continually seeketh her lost children.}}∷ vvoman hauing ten grotes: if she leese one grote, doth she not light a candle, and sweepe the house, and seeke diligently, vntil she finde? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=9}}† And vvhen she hath found, calleth together her frendes and neighbours, saying, Reioyce vvith me, because I haue found the grote vvhich I had lost? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=10}}† So, I say to you, there shal be ioy {{sup|‖}} before the Angels of God vpon one sinner that doth penance.⊣

{{verse|chapter=15|verse=11}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Saturday in the 2 weeke of Lent.}}And he said, A certaine man had tvvo sonnes: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=12}}† and the yonger of them said to his father, Father, giue me the portion of substance that belongeth to me. And he deuided vnto them the substance. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The prodigal sonne, is a parable, both of the Gentils conuersion, & also of euery dissolute sinner penitently returning to God.}}∷ And not many daies after the yonger sonne gathering al his things together vvent from home into a farre countrie: and there he wasted his substance, liuing riotously. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=14}}† And after he had spent al, there fel a sore famine in that countrie, and he began to be in neede. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=15}}† And he vvent, and cleaued to one of the citizens of that countrie. And he sent him into his farme to feede svvine. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=16}}† And he vvould faine haue filled his bellie of the huskes that the svvine did eate: and no bodie gaue vnto him. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=17}}† And returning to him self he said, Hovv many of my fathers hirelings haue aboundance of bread: and I here perish for famine? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=18}}† I vvil arise, and vvil goe to my father, and say to him, Father, I haue sinned against heauen and before thee: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=19}}† I am not novv vvorthie to be called thy sonne: make me as one of thy hirelings. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=20}}† And rising vp he came to his father. And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Gods wonderful and tender mercie toward penitent sinners.}}∷ vvhen he vvas yet farre of, his father savv him, and vvas moued vvith mercie, and running to him fel vpon his necke, and kissed him. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=21}}† And his sonne said to him, Father, I haue sinned against heauen & before thee, I am not novv vvorthie to be called thy sonne. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=22}}† And the father said to his seruants, Quickely bring forth the first stole, and doe it on him, and put a ring vpon his hand, and shoes vpon his feete: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=23}}† and bring {{sup|‖}} the fatted calfe, and kil it, and let vs eate, and make merie: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=24}}† because this my sonne vvas dead, and is reuiued: vvas lost, and is found. And they began to make merie. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=25}}† But his elder sonne vvas in the field.<noinclude>{{rh|||and}}</noinclude>
